_comment: Bibliographic manifest for the paper-validation folders. DOIs/titles verified against Crossref (api.crossref.org). Read by scripts/docs/gen_validation_page.py.

papers.label: Arora & Hasan (2021)
papers.citation: A. Arora, M.M.F. Hasan, Flexible oxygen concentrators for medical applications, Scientific Reports 11 (2021) 14317.
papers.system: O2/N2 (air) on LiLSX, 4-step PSA and PVSA
findings: O2 purity is within about 4 percentage points of Table 4, but recovery is far below the paper (4 % vs 30 % for PSA, 20 % vs 66 % for PVSA). This is an open disagreement, not a tuned result.

The paper's recovery is a model value from an optimiser; the t1/t4 rows of the PSA column of Table 4 were lost in the text extraction (t1 = 3.0 s is an estimate). The isotherm form is the non-competitive dual-site Langmuir; the paper does not state whether its DSL is competitive, so it was left as is.
The PSA deck now vents the depressurisation step counter-currently (feed end), as the paper states for every Table 4 case; it previously vented co-currently.

papers.label: Casas et al. (2012) / Schell et al. (2012)
papers.citation: N. Casas, J. Schell, R. Pini, M. Mazzotti, Fixed bed adsorption of CO2/H2 mixtures on activated carbon: experiments and modeling, Adsorption 18 (2012) 143-161; J. Schell, N. Casas, R. Pini, M. Mazzotti, Pure and binary adsorption of CO2, H2, and N2 on activated carbon, Adsorption 18 (2012) 49-65.
papers.system: CO2/H2 breakthrough on activated carbon AP3-60
papers.reference_kind: paper's simulated breakthrough times (Table 5); isotherm fits (Schell Table 3)
findings: CO2 breakthrough times agree with the paper's simulated Table 5 values to 0.5-1.3 % for the 50/50 and 25/75 feeds and 13 % for 75/25; H2 breakthrough is 15-19 % early for the two CO2-lean feeds.

Table 5 is the paper's simulation (feed velocity fitted per experiment, piping to the mass spectrometer modelled); adsim uses the 10 cm3/s set-point and no piping. The experimental curves (Figs. 4, 6) have not been digitised.
The competitive Arrhenius-Sips isotherm reproduces the paper's per-temperature Sips fits (Schell et al., Table 3) to 7 % (CO2) and 0.6 % (H2).

papers.label: Ferré et al. (2026)
papers.citation: A. Ferré, C. Wedler, A. Ward, J. Burger, R. Pini, C. Petit, Co-production of high-purity carbon dioxide and methane via a single-bed pressure-vacuum swing adsorption process, Separation and Purification Technology 406 (2026) 138821.
findings: Product purities agree with Table 5 within 0.1-1.8 percentage points and CO2 recovery within 0.6-3 pp; CH4 recovery is 5-7 pp low for the zeolites and 11 pp high for MIL-160(Al), whose CH4 productivity is 59 % high.

The decks now use the extended (competitive) DSL isotherm the paper states (Sect. 3.1); they previously used the non-competitive form. adsim uses a constant LDF coefficient and a single heat of adsorption per component instead of the paper's loading-dependent forms.
Specific energy is not compared: the decks drive the pressure steps with pressure boundary conditions, not pump models.

papers.label: Haghpanah et al. (2013) / Glover et al. (2026)
papers.citation: R. Haghpanah, A. Majumder, R. Nilam, A. Rajendran, S. Farooq, I.A. Karimi, M. Amanullah, Multiobjective optimization of a four-step adsorption process for postcombustion CO2 capture via finite volume simulation, Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research 52 (2013) 4249-4265; T. Glover, T. Papathanasiou, R. Pini, Accelerating simulation and optimisation of cyclic adsorption processes with differentiable programming, arXiv:2606.21523 (2026).
papers.system: CO2/N2 4-step PVSA on zeolite 13X (pressurisation, adsorption, forward blowdown, reverse evacuation)
papers.reference_kind: paper's own model results (Sect. 6.1, Table 6); Glover et al.'s re-implementation of the same model (Table 4) and its CSS multiplier
findings: On the five minimum-energy designs of Table 6, CO2 purity and recovery agree with Glover et al.'s verification runs within 1.6 percentage points and the productivity within 3.4 %. The specific energy is 0.7-6 % above Haghpanah's Table 6 for evacuation pressures of 0.05-0.1 bar but 12 % above at 0.02-0.03 bar, where nearly all of it is vacuum work.

The energy gap and the Sect. 6.1 purity (79.7 % against 88.74 %; recovery matches within 1.6 pp) are open. Grid, heat-of-adsorption value and convention, wall heat transfer and dispersion closure move them by under 0.3 pp or 1 %; the unit basis of q* in the paper's loading-dependent LDF coefficient (Eq. 40) moves the energy into agreement only at the cost of the Sect. 6.1 recovery (README).
The dominant multiplier of the cycle map at Glover et al.'s benchmark design, fitted from the decay of the end-of-cycle state change on 10 cells, is 0.9513 against Glover's 0.9509.

papers.label: Nguyen et al. (2022)
papers.citation: T.T.T. Nguyen, J.-B. Lin, G.K.H. Shimizu, A. Rajendran, Separation of CO2 and N2 on a hydrophobic metal organic framework CALF-20, Chemical Engineering Journal 442 (2022) 136263.
papers.system: CO2/He and CO2/N2 breakthrough on CALF-20 (six runs of Figs. 4 and 5)
papers.reference_kind: measured markers re-digitised from Figs. 4 and 5 (outlet y_CO2, y_N2, thermocouple); the paper's model curves (code to code)
findings: The curves used until 2026-11-12 as the experiment were the paper's model lines, digitised; the measured markers were re-digitised from the 300 dpi figures, with each run's flow, temperature and pressure from the author's thesis (Table A2.1). Fig. 5 is a CO2/N2 feed (the decks fed CO2 in helium before).

With the paper's parameters and model forms (nothing fitted), the CO2 fronts are +6.5, +3.2, +10.9 % (Fig. 4: 100, 70, 50 % CO2) and -7.2, +5.6, -9.7 % (Fig. 5: 30, 15, 5 %) from the measurements; the paper's own model is +7.6, +5.0, +15.4, -9.6, +10.0, -5.8 %. Code to code the fronts agree with the paper's model within 0.1-4.1 %.

Fig. 5 thermocouple RMSE 1.0-2.7 K and outlet N2 RMSE 0.04-0.28; the Fig. 4 temperature peaks are 6-8 K above the measurement and 5-6 K above the paper's model (open item). Calibrating the thermal values on Fig. 4, as the paper did, makes the Fig. 5 temperatures worse, so no calibration is shipped. The particle diameter (1.5 mm, pellets 1-3 mm) and the wall-end condition are assumptions.

papers.label: Nguyen et al. (2023)
papers.citation: T.T.T. Nguyen, G.K.H. Shimizu, A. Rajendran, CO2/N2 separation by vacuum swing adsorption using a metal-organic framework, CALF-20: Multi-objective optimization and experimental validation, Chemical Engineering Journal 452 (2023) 139550.
papers.system: CO2/N2 VSA on CALF-20 (4-step and LPP)
findings: Four-step cycles (I-V): CO2 purity within 1.7-4.9 pp and recovery within 1.2-2.7 pp of the experiments; productivity within 5-9 %.

LPP cycles (VI-X): purity within 0.2-2.7 pp of the experiments, but recovery is 7-10 pp high and exceeds 100 % for IX and X, at the cyclic steady state of the per-component mass balance (VIII-X need about 300-500 cycles to reach it). The single-bed emulation couples the light-product pressurisation to the feed step by composition, not by moles, so CO2 enters through the LPP stream that is not drawn from the raffinate; this is a limitation of the deck/connection model, recorded rather than hidden.

The decks now use the competitive DSL form (as the paper's ref. [10]); the paper's column length (0.267 m) is inconsistent with its adsorbent mass and particle density, and the deck keeps the mass (L = 0.304 m).

papers.citation: T.T.T. Nguyen, G.K.H. Shimizu, A. Rajendran, Experimental demonstration of humid post-combustion CO2 capture by vacuum swing adsorption using CALF-20, Adsorption 31 (2025) 45.
findings: Dry case B0 (the operating point of Nguyen 2023 Exp. VII): CO2 purity within 0.9 pp and productivity within 2 % of Table 1, inside the printed uncertainty; the productivity agreement is partly compensation, because the engine's recovery is 11.6 pp high. Dry case A0: purity 3.4 pp low (recorded).

Recovery is about 11 pp high in both cases, the light-product over-recovery of the Nguyen 2023 LPP decks; none of the printed parameters closes it (README attribution: the SI's fitted blowdown and evacuation decay rates lower it by up to 5 pp and raise the purity, the measured 0.267 m column raises it by about 2 pp). A0's printed productivity is inconsistent with its own cycle time and is recorded, not asserted.

The decks are the Nguyen2023_Exp_VII deck at 0.96 bar and 22 C. The main text was not read here (the SI was); the humid cases are not reproduced: the paper prints no water isotherm, and the engine has no competitive CO2/H2O kind for a physisorbent (#272).
papers.label: Nguyen et al. (2025)
papers.reference_kind: experimental purity/recovery/productivity of the dry cases (Table 1)
papers.system: CO2/N2 VSA with light-product pressurisation on CALF-20 (dry cases of a humid-feed study)

papers.label: Estupiñan Perez et al. (2019)
papers.citation: L. Estupiñan Perez, P. Sarkar, A. Rajendran, Experimental validation of multi-objective optimization techniques for design of vacuum swing adsorption processes, Separation and Purification Technology 224 (2019) 553-563.
papers.system: CO2/N2 VSA on zeolite 13X (4-step and LPP)
findings: The decks use the paper's model forms (WP10 audit of the paper and SI, 2026-10-31): the two-term exponential evacuation pressure of Sect. 4.3 (0.019 and 0.101 1/s; the split of the terms is not printed and an equal split is used, chosen on A), wall ends at ambient (SI Table S2), the Blake-Kozeny pressure drop (Ergun) and the capacity-factor LDF of SI Eq. S4. Four-step cycles: CO2 purity within 0.2-0.6 pp and recovery within 0.7-1.1 pp of experiments A and B (recovery was 8-10 pp high); C1 is 4.5 pp below its experiment and 12 pp below the repeat C2, which differ from each other by 7 pp. LPP cycles: purity 1.5-3.3 pp low and recovery 1.9-3.3 pp high.

Attribution (README): the four-step recovery excess was the evacuation pressure history. The paper's profile keeps the column above P_low for most of the 57 s step where the deck's single exponential reached it; the capacity-factor kinetics, the wall ends and the pressure-drop constant are each worth under 0.5 pp. The LPP cycles' 167 s evacuation reaches P_low whatever the profile; their remaining recovery excess is the composition-coupled LPP connection.

Open: the split of the two evacuation terms (Fig. 6c would pin it); the experiment ended steps on pressure triggers whose durations are not printed; the one-second hold between steps and about 5 % dead volume are not modelled.

papers.label: Streb & Mazzotti (2021)
papers.citation: A. Streb, M. Mazzotti, Adsorption for efficient low carbon hydrogen production: part 1 - adsorption equilibrium and breakthrough studies for H2/CO2/CH4 on zeolite 13X, Adsorption 27 (2021) 541-558.
papers.system: CO2/CH4 and H2/CO2/CH4 breakthrough on zeolite 13X
papers.reference_kind: digitised experimental outlet compositions and thermocouples (Figs. 6, 7, 11); decks calibrated on A3
findings: The decks are calibrated on A3 alone: CO2 and CH4 LDF coefficients 0.0592 and 0.137 1/s (Table 4: 0.06, 0.2), wall-to-thermofluid coefficient 49.7 W/(m2 K) (paper 220) and a 0.142 L plug-flow sampling line to the MS (an inert, nearly empty layer above the bed). Each other case is a prediction except its feed flow, which is fitted to the speed of its own CO2 temperature front (as the paper fits the velocity per experiment). CO2 fronts are within 1.4 % of the experiments and CH4 fronts within 2.4 % (B1 4.7 % early); outlet NRMSE 1.3-16 % (CO2) and 4.7-31 % (CH4); thermocouple RMSE 5.5-11.4 K. Before: 0.3-11 %, 0.2-18 %, 2.4-45 %, 13-84 % and 8.7-28.5 K.

Six flow factors exceed 2 % of the set point (A1 +5.1, A2 -6.1, A4 -9.4, A6 -3.5, B1 +5.7, B2 -11.3 %). The paper's bound is 2 % of the MFC full scale, which is not printed: with a full scale of at least 31 NL/min every case but A4 is inside it. Held to 2 % of the set point, A1, A2, A4, B1 and B2 keep front errors of 3-10 % (README).

The engine's void region is one well-mixed cell, which smears the CH4 front, so the line is a multi-cell inert layer. The decks keep extended Sips competition; IAST, recorded on the same calibrated decks, puts the CO2 fronts 0.3-11 % late.

papers.label: Vysyaraju et al. (2024)
papers.citation: R. Vysyaraju, J.A. Sawada, L. Estupiñan Perez, A. Rajendran, Simulation and experimental demonstration of helium purification from He/N2 mixtures by pressure swing adsorption, Chemical Engineering Journal 499 (2024) 155929.
papers.system: He/N2 on zeolite 5A: breakthrough and 5-step PSA
papers.reference_kind: experimental values stated in the text and Table 3
findings: The N2 breakthrough loadings match the reported value (ambient) and the DSL value (11.2 bar) to 2-4 %, and the peak bed temperature to 0.3 K.

He purity is 0.54 pp below the paper model (1.4 pp above the experiment), and He recovery is 63 % against 31 %: the deck is a single bed with self-equalisation, the experiment and the paper's model are a 3-bed cycle.

papers.label: Ward & Pini (2022)
papers.citation: A. Ward, R. Pini, Integrated uncertainty quantification and sensitivity analysis of single-component dynamic column breakthrough experiments, Adsorption 28 (2022) 161-183.
papers.system: CO2 breakthrough on activated carbon at 50/100/200 ccm
papers.reference_kind: digitised experimental outlet composition and thermocouple
findings: The decks use the paper's model forms (WP10 audit, 2026-10-31: helium carrier, the paper's dispersion correlation Eq. 4 with D_m = 0.605e-5 m2/s, -dU_1 + RT as the heat of adsorption, the wall ends held at ambient (Table 4), the Ergun pressure drop) with four values calibrated against the digitised curves of all three flows (2026-11): the ambient and wall-end temperature 293 K (Table 1: 291.4 K; the thermocouple settles at 293 K after the front), q_s,2 5.89 mol/kg (Table 2: 6.04, inside the paper's 95 % interval), the factor 3.75 on Eq. 4 (the paper fits 4) and h_in 97.3 / 81.5 / 69.0 W/(m2 K) (Table 6: 77.5 / 57.9 / 45.2). The CO2 front is within 0.4 % of the measurement, the outlet NRMSE 2.7-3.9 % and the thermocouple RMSE 0.18-1.40 K (before the calibration: 1.7-4.5 % late, 14-35 % and 1.15-2.56 K).

Attribution (one change at a time, README): the 293 K ambient alone brings the front to within 0.7-1.6 %, q_s,2 closes the rest, the larger h_in takes out the extra heat and the dispersion factor sets the front width. The calibration is fitted to the same digitised curves it is compared with, so it is not an independent validation. Of the audit's changes, the fitted dispersion factor halves the temperature rise and the wall end condition moves the front from early to late; the carrier gas, the RT term and the pressure-drop constant are each worth under 1 % in the front time.

Every deck value is traced to the paper in the README's provenance table. The deck keeps the particle voidage at 0 in the gas holdup (the paper's balances count the bed voidage only) and uses 60 cells to the paper's 30.

papers.label: Ward & Pini (2024)
papers.citation: A. Ward, R. Pini, Design and Performance Evaluation of Multisorbent Vacuum-Swing Adsorption Processes for Postcombustion Carbon Capture, Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research 63 (2024) 13787-13800.
findings: CO2 purity within 2.3 pp, recovery within 1.8 pp and productivity within 0.7 % of Table 4.
The deck now uses the extended (competitive) DSL the paper states (Sect. 2.1). Energy is not compared (no pump model in the deck).

papers.label: Halabi (2011)
papers.citation: M.H. Halabi, Sorption enhanced catalytic reforming of methane for pure hydrogen production: experimental and modeling, PhD thesis, Eindhoven University of Technology, 2011 (chapters 8 and 9).
papers.system: Sorption-enhanced steam methane reforming: Rh/Ce0.6Zr0.4O2 catalyst mixed with K2CO3-promoted hydrotalcite, 450 C, 1.5-6 bar
papers.reference_kind: thesis's computed gas-phase equilibria (Fig. 7 legend, Table 6); measured conversion and H2 (Table 6, recorded only)
findings: With an inert sorbent the chapter-8 rate model (LHHW, the two site balances expanded into one denominator) reaches the thesis's printed equilibria: Fig. 7 within 0.46 pp, the Table 6 equilibrium column within 1.95 pp. The model equals a direct solution of the two equilibria with the thesis's K values; the Table 6 column lies 0.3-2.0 pp below it.

The sorption-enhanced runs are recorded, not asserted. The model's conversion has no plateau before breakthrough, and CO2 breaks through after 1.6-3.4 min against the thesis's 4-15 min. A 60 s reading seemed to agree at 1.5 bar, but that is an artefact of the read time.
The open input is the sorbent capacity below 0.05 bar CO2: the thesis's Freundlich fit (0.13 mol/kg at 0.024 bar), its Table 3 and its Henry constant disagree by up to 2x (skarstrom#245).
